questions.title: Who will top the men's javelin throw qualification standings at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.background: The men's javelin throw competition includes a qualifying round before the final.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Games results for the overall men's javelin throw qualification at the 2026 Commonwealth Games Resolution Date : July 30, 2026 Accepted Answer Format : Full name of the athlete ranked first in the overall men's javelin throw qualification results
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-26 form and fitness update for Glasgow men's javelin qualification on July 30 (Hindustan Times/PTI July 26, Rediff/Telangana Today July 26, The News Pakistan July 15, OCA Asia July 23): Contrary to earlier assumptions that reigning Olympic/CWG champion Arshad Nadeem was in peak form, PTI reports he 'has been struggling for some time' and enters Glasgow off an 'extremely poor 78.47m effort at Luzern, Switzerland, on July 16'—a European tune-up where he specifically aimed to test form—slashing his qualification-topper odds (0.19 -> 0.08), especially given his historically conservative qualifying rounds. Conversely, Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage (92.62m Rome DL world leader, three additional 88m+ throws, two 2026 DL titles) dominates 2026 form by >5.5m (0.28 -> 0.34). India's Neeraj Chopra (85.69m Doha DL June 19 after back/groin rehab; arrived Glasgow July 24, head coach calls him in 'perfect physical shape', renowned Throw-1 qualifier thriving in forecast Glasgow rain/wind) rises into clear #2 (0.20 -> 0.23), healthy Rabat DL winner Anderson Peters (86.38m SB, strong qualifier) climbs to #3 (0.11 -> 0.14), and Commonwealth #2 season leader Rohit Yadav (87.05m SB, moderated by a July 15 Lucerne knee withdrawal) edges up (0.05 -> 0.06), leaving 15% residual for Keshorn Walcott (83.45m SB), Julius Yego, Yashvir Singh, and windy 3-throw auto-Q variance.

questions.title: Which candidate will receive the most “encourage” votes in the first UN Security Council straw poll of the 2026 secretary-general selection?
questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.

(2) Macky Sall trims 0.07 -> 0.05 after Ugandan former UN USG Olara Otunnu formally entered on July 24-26 as the 7th candidate, breaking Sall's solo-African status (partially offset by Gabon President Oligui Nguema's July 25 unity endorsement) and widening residual for Espinosa + Otunnu from 0.02 to 0.03. (3) Reuters and Geneva Solutions (July 26) reiterate diplomats see 'no obvious frontrunner' amid strong norms for a Latin American and first female SG, narrowing Rafael Grossi's slight lead (0.43 -> 0.41) over Rebeca Grynspan (0.36 -> 0.37), while Michelle Bachelet trims 0.04 -> 0.03 as today's July 27 US UNSC walkout over UN rights chief Volker Turk underscores acute US hostility toward UNHCHR alumni alongside her China/Chile hurdles.

No secretariat staff will be present and the ballot papers are shredded at the end of the voting, after which the UN General Assembly and the media will be informed that a straw poll has taken place but will not receive any further details. The UN charter says the secretary general, who is the chief administrative officer and the most senior diplomat in the UN, is elected by the general assembly, where all member states are represented, on a recommendation from the UN Security Council. In practice, the security council chooses a candidate during a series of straw polls that will continue from this week until September or October before submitting the name to the general assembly for a rubber stamp. questions.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Rule : Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-27/28 breaking escalation (Reuters/SRNA, Mediafax, Romania Insider, CEENERGYNEWS, Daily News Hungary, Montel News, AFP/Straits Times): Following an emergency Energy Command meeting chaired by PM & interim Energy Minister Ilie Bolojan, Romania's state-owned Nuclearelectrica executed a controlled shutdown of Unit 1 at Cernavoda (1 of 2 reactors at Romania's sole nuclear plant) at 11:00 a.m. on July 28 after Danube flow plunged to a 30-year low of ~1,630 m3/s; Unit 1 will not restart before August 4 at the earliest, and Nuclearelectrica explicitly warned it may also shut down Unit 2 (completing a full plant shutdown, with only a ~15 cm margin between Unit 1/2 limits) if levels fall further. Meanwhile, upstream Danube levels just broke all-time records in Budapest (31 cm, July 28) and at Paks (-106 cm, July 27), propagating downstream toward Cernavoda over the next 2-4 days as another heatwave approaches. Surging Romania 0.38 -> 0.74 (+0.36). Hungary trims 0.26 -> 0.16: Paks only curtailed Unit 1 by 254 MW (~13% of its 4-unit plant) late July 27 and requires another ~25-30 cm drop for a full 4-unit shutdown, though Economy/Energy Minister Istvan Kapitany warned of further falling water and heat. Bulgaria (Kozloduy, 0.13 -> 0.05) moves ahead of Slovenia (Krsko, 0.21 -> 0.03) because a Viking cruise ship grounded near Vidin on July 28 due to low Danube water (confirming acute local drought, though zero Kozloduy curbs yet), while Krsko had zero late-July cooling alerts after July 21 storms and auxiliary cooling towers. Belarus holds at 0.01 (sum 0.99).

questions.title: Who will win the men's javelin throw gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.background: The 2026 Commonwealth Games are scheduled to take place in Glasgow, Scotland.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Commonwealth Games results or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the gold medallist in the 2026 men's javelin throw final. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete declared the gold medallist at the conclusion of the final. Subsequent medal reallocations will not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The gold medallist's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-26 form and fitness update ahead of the July 31 Glasgow men's javelin final (Hindustan Times/PTI July 26, Rediff/Telangana Today July 26, The News Pakistan July 15, OCA Asia July 23): Arshad Nadeem's 'extremely poor 78.47m' at his July 16 Lucerne tune-up—amid reports he 'has been struggling for some time'—forces a sharp downgrade from #2 to #4 (0.23 -> 0.11, retaining 11% for his 92.97m Olympic-champion peaking ceiling across 6 final throws). Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage strengthens as clear gold favorite (0.33 -> 0.40) as the sole 90m+ thrower globally in 2026 (92.62m Rome DL + three other 88m+ throws + two DL titles), moderated below 0.45 by first major-championship final pressure and forecast Glasgow rain/gusty winds. Neeraj Chopra (0.19 -> 0.22, new #2) returns to Glasgow reporting 'I feel much better now' and 'perfect physical shape' per head coach Radhakrishnan Nair after a month of Swiss rehab following his June 19 Doha return (85.69m) and Lucerne groin caution. Healthy 2026 Rabat DL champion Anderson Peters (86.38m SB, 2x World Champion) rises into #3 (0.10 -> 0.14), reigning world champion Keshorn Walcott holds at 0.05 (83.45m SB, yet to peak), leaving 8% residual for Rohit Yadav (87.05m SB, recovering from July 15 knee issue), Julius Yego, and field.
